THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Challenging judgment and award dated 22.07.2015 passed by II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT at Kalaburagi (for short 'tribunal') in MVC no.1316/2009, this appeal is filed.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT at Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Smt.Preeti Patil Melkundi, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal was by insurer challenging award of tribunal as being contrary to terms of remand passed by this Court in MFA no.30114/2012 (MV) disposed of on 08.12.2014.

It was submitted that as per claimant, on 27.02.2009, when he was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-32/Q-3458 near Hanuman Temple, another vehicle bearing registration no.KA-32/U-5866 came from opposite direction and dashed against it due to NC: 2023:KHC-K:7492 rash and negligent riding by its rider.
In said accident, claimant sustained grievous injuries.
Despite taking treatment, he did not recover fully and sustained permanent physical disability.
Claiming compensation for same, he filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act (for short 'M.V. Act') against owner and insurer of vehicle.
3. On service of notice, owner and insurer entered appearance and opposed claim petition.
Based on pleadings, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence of claimant as PW.1 and Dr.Shubhash Shah as PW.2.
Exs.P1 to P12 were marked.

On behalf of respondents, official of insurer was examined as RW.1 and got marked copy of insurance policy as Ex.R1.
4.

On consideration, tribunal had initially passed award on 21.09.2011 dismissing claim petition on ground that as per claimant, accident occurred on 27.02.2009, but complaint based on which FIR was registered, was lodged on 27.07.2009 i.e., after delay of five months.

Therefore, NC:
2023:KHC-K:7492 tribunal disbelieved evidence of claimant and dismissed claim petition.

sentences.text: said award, claimant preferred appeal before this Court in MFA no.30114/2012.

Said appeal was disposed of on 08.12.2014 remitting matter back to tribunal with specific directions as follows:
"Appeal is allowed.
The judgment and award dated 21.09.2011 passed in MVC no.1316/2011 by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge & MACT at Gulbarga are set aside.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge & MACT at Gulbarga
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Matter is remitted to the Tribunal to give comprehensive finding on issue nos.2 and 3 after getting MLC Register from Sanjot Hospital and if possible, summoning the police Officer, who conducted the investigation and filed the charge-sheet."
5. After remand however, no further evidence was led either by claimant or insurer.

On consideration, tribunal passed impugned order holding insurer liable to pay compensation on ground that there was sufficient material to presume actionable negligence against respondents and there was no contrary evidence led.

It was submitted that when reason for remanding matter to NC:
2023:KHC-K:7492 tribunal was with direction to tribunal to summon MLC Register from Sanjot Hospital, tribunal ought not to have decided matter based on available material.

Therefore,
impugned award was passed without following direction issued by this Court.
Hence, sought for allowing appeal.
6. Though matter was passed over, there is no appearance on behalf of respondent no.1.
Since matter is of year 2015, it is taken up for final disposal.

7. From above submission and since insurer is in appeal challenging award on question of liability,
point that would arise for consideration is:
 "Whether impugned award calls for  interference?
8.

On perusal of judgment dated 08.12.2014 in MFA no.30114/2012, it is seen that claimant had examined himself and Dr. Shubhash Shah as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P12, while insurer examined its official as RW.1 and got marked insurance policy as Ex.R1.

Though remand was with specific direction to tribunal to secure MLC records from Sanjot Hospoital to find corroboration about occurrence of accident involving insured vehicle, without parties leading further evidence and without tribunal securing copy of MLC Register from Sanjot Hospital, it proceeded to dispose of matter based on available material.

Since it was observed by this Court that available material would be inconclusive regarding occurrence of accident as claimed by claimant, holding actionable negligence established against appellant-insurer based on material which was already considered would be untenable.
Therefore, point for consideration is answered in affirmative.
9. In view of above finding, impugned award is required to be set-aside and matter remitted back to tribunal.

Consequently, following:

sentences.text:
Appeal is allowed in part, impugned judgment and award is set aside.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:7492 ii.
Matter is remanded back to tribunal for fresh consideration strictly in accordance with directions issued by this court in MFA no.30114/2012 and to pass fresh award.
iii. Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to tribunal subject to outcome of claim petition.
iv. To facilitate early disposal, parties i.e., appellant and respondent no.1-claimant shall appear before Tribunal on 30.10.2023 without awaiting fresh notice.
v. Registry to draw award and transmit Trial Court Records to tribunal, before 30.10.2023.
vi. Tribunal is requested to dispose of claim petition on priority as far as possible, but in any case within an outer limit of six months.
vii. All contentions kept open.
